title: Letter 42 — Patience and Heavenly Consolation
attribution_note: Letter 42 of 46 in the collection Letters Sent — see Letter 1 for provenance.

sections.heading: In your patience possess your souls

pairs.en: Remember that God saith unto them that would be saved: *“In your patience possess ye your souls.”* [Luke 21:19]

Read in the Apocalypse chapters 2 and 3, and chapter 7 from verse 9 unto the end of the chapter, and chapter 19, and chapter 20, and chapters 21 and 22. There is opened the blessedness of the higher life, and the joy, and the triumph, and the glory which is to be given unto the elect of God in the age to come.

Christ saith: *“Behold, I come as a thief.* *Blessed is he that watcheth, and keepeth his garments, lest he walk naked, and they see his shame.”* [Revelation 16:15] Endure all that may befall you, that in eternal life ye may receive refreshment. And for your parents pray diligently unto God, that He may have mercy on them.

sections.heading: God leaves us not without consolation

pairs.en: For the strengthening of your faint-heartedness I write that this week, in our monastery, one heard something, when he had lain down to sleep and at the very midnight had but just dozed off: namely, he heard such singing from above, over him, that his heart from joy and sweetness melted as wax; and as soon as the singing was ended, he awoke, and felt in his heart such joy and sweetness as remained with him for a time, and soon departed from him. And then there came upon him a great sorrow, that that joy had gone from him. Consider this yourselves, and make it known unto your brethren in Christ. God leaves us not even here without consolation. And how then shall He comfort us in the age to come! Therefore endure all things, and strive to please Christ in all.
